Hi Jasmine —

Starting ~08:50 PST we saw a sharp spike of 5xx and 429 responses from calls to Redwood for our Clinical Assist feature. Could you confirm whether this is an incident on Redwood's side and whether you have mitigations now? We need an ETA for recovery and any workaround (pin to another model or region, etc.).

Thanks,
Tom

Tom — thanks for flagging and for the logs. I'm escalating immediately. Initial read: the pattern looks like a retry amplification (lots of concurrent short-lived retries) plus several long tail 5xx bursts consistent with GPU pool saturation in the us-west dedicated cluster that serves your pool.

Immediate actions we've kicked off:
- Opening an incident with SRE and paging on-call.
- Temporarily routing your traffic to a standby variant in a different pool while we stabilize (this will increase latency slightly but should reduce 5xxs).
- Capturing a sample of requests for root cause analysis.

I'll loop you back within 30 minutes with the mitigation status and next steps.

—Jasmine

Subject: [Internal] Pelican Health - 5xx/429 spike — immediate triage

Team — Pelican Health is reporting a spike of 5xx/429s and retry storms hitting Clinical Assist since 08:50 PST. They own a dedicated capacity pool (us-west-dedicated-phi) and we've got signs of GPU capacity exhaustion + autoscaler lag. Tom attached logs (see thread).

Ask:
- Laura: can you confirm current node utilization and any recent evictions for us-west-dedicated-phi? Any autoscale throttling logs?
- Rishi: can we instantiate a fallback route to the standby pool and pin Pelican traffic there? Also please confirm TTL for KV cache and whether prefix caching will survive the route change.
- Monica: please coordinate comms and put together a short customer-facing incident note.

Priorities: stop the retry amplification + get Pelican stable ASAP. I'll update Tom in 30.

--
Jasmine
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 09:28:03 -0800
Subject: Re: [Internal] Pelican Health - 5xx/429 spike — immediate triage

On Tue, Dec 7, 2026 at 09:22 AM PST jasmine_liu@redwood.ai wrote:
> Team — Pelican Health is reporting a spike...

We're seeing sustained GPU exhaustion on pool us-west-dedicated-phi. Summary:
- Node saturation started ~08:44 PST, concurrent queued requests per replica >200.
- Autoscaler attempted +3 node scale at 08:46 but one of the queued resizes failed due to insufficient spare capacity in the farm (allocation conflict).
- At 08:51 we observed cache eviction (KV) leading to more cold starts.

Mitigations applied (in progress):
- Forced warm failover: rerouted Pelican to us-west-standby-1 (different cluster) at 09:25 PST. Traffic now routed but we see an initial tail of retries causing continuing 429s.
- We raised a short-term quota to allow additional ephemeral nodes; still provisioning.
- Collecting kernel traces and autoscaler logs; attaching CSV timeline (autoscale-timeline.csv).

Next: coordinate with Rishi on client-side backoff suggestions and consider temporary request rate-limiting at the edge to break the retry loop.

Laura Bennett
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 09:46:10 -0800
Subject: Re: [Internal] Pelican Health - 5xx/429 spike — immediate triage

Quick notes from runtime/serving:
- Root cause (preliminary): sudden shift in Pelican's request distribution (more long-context chat sessions) + a batch of concurrent health-check retries from their side created a hot prefix that consumed GPU KV memory; the autoscaler is tuned to avoid oscillation and the scale decision took ~120s to commit, by which point queues were building up -> 5xx/429 burst.
- Short-term mitigations we pushed at 09:25–09:40 PST:
  * Route to standby model/capacity (Laura executed).
  * Applied soft rate-limit at the ingress (50% of current qps) to break retry amplification.
  * TTL for KV cache extended for Pelican model to reduce cold-starts on failover.
- Longer-term recommendations to propose to customer:
  * Move to a small warm standby pool for mission-critical endpoints (reserved capacity).
  * Enable client-side jittered exponential backoff and circuit breaker around 429s to avoid retry storms.
  * We'll propose a quantized model variant with smaller KV footprint for high-concurrency sessions.

I'll join the customer call in 30.

Rishi Malhotra
Principal, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Spike of 5xx/429s impacting Clinical Assist - urgent

Tom — quick update and mitigation plan:

What happened (short):
- A combination of increased long-context sessions and a burst of client retries created a hot working set that exhausted GPU KV inside the us-west dedicated pool. The autoscaler initiated scale but the allocation encountered a conflict and was delayed ~2 minutes, during which queues overflowed producing 5xx and 429 responses.

What we did (now):
- Rerouted your traffic to a standby pool (us-west-standby-1) — traffic is flowing but you may see slightly higher latency for a short window.
- Applied ingress rate-limiting to break the retry loop.
- Increased TTL on KV cache to reduce cold-start penalties.

Immediate ask for Pelican:
- Please apply jittered exponential backoff on retries and temporarily reduce aggressive health-check rates. This will stop the amplification while we stabilize.

Next steps and ETA:
- We're collecting logs and will provide a post-incident summary within 48 hours.
- Recommended follow-up: schedule a short architecture review to discuss a reserved standby pool and a lighter-weight model variant for high-concurrency sessions.

Monica will share the customer-facing incident note shortly and coordinate credits if needed. Sorry for the disruption — we're treating this as a high-priority incident.

—Jasmine

Tom — thanks again for patience. Quick follow-up after our stabilization yesterday:

Summary:
- Incident window: 2026-12-07 08:44 — 2026-12-07 09:30 PST.
- Root cause (prelim): GPU KV working set exhaustion in us-west-dedicated-phi + autoscale allocation conflict -> retry amplification and 5xx/429 burst.
- Impact: elevated 5xx/429s and higher latencies for Clinical Assist; affected a subset of pilot customers.

Actions taken:
- Forced failover to us-west-standby-1 and ingress rate-limiting to break retries.
- Extended KV TTL and increased ephemeral node quota while we evaluate capacity planning.
- Engineering is preparing a follow-up proposal (architecture changes + reserved warm standby).

Deliverables & timeline:
- Post-incident report (including timeline, logs, and mitigation notes) — 48 hours.
- Proposed risk reduction plan (options + costs for reserved capacity and quantized model) — 5 business days.

If you'd like, we can schedule an executive readout and include cost mitigation options in the proposal. Please let me know availability.
